key_insight: SciConsolidate turns verified execution traces into transferable procedural knowledge, then uses a stronger model to convert that knowledge into executable supervision so smaller models can actually benefit.
engineering_relevance: For scientific and solid mechanics workflows, this offers a practical path to make LLMs better at reusing successful computational strategies across related problems instead of overfitting to one-off fixes.
method: Contrast verified successes vs. failures to synthesize cross-task procedures
Use a development-validation gate to keep only robust procedures
Generate failure-informed, answer-free queries and concretize procedures with a stronger teacher for procedure-free SFT
evidence_signal: On SciCode, procedure injection improved Qwen3.6-27B by +3.85/+6.26 on sub-step/main-problem scores, and procedure-guided concretization improved the 9B student by +3.89/+6.25 over no-procedure SFT and +5.62/+11.25 over the original model.
watch_item: The approach depends on a stronger teacher to operationalize abstractions, so gains may be limited when the target model cannot execute procedures or when teacher-generated concretization does not transfer cleanly.
paper_title: From Execution to Capability: Scientific Experience Consolidation via Procedural Knowledge Synthesis
